sentence: This project studies how cytotoxic T cells kill tumor cells again and again, using CRISPR screens to find genes that control this.
This project gathers scientists to discuss how a virus, the immune response, human genetics and environmental factors together cause nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
This project tries to find out how genetic changes that hinder repair of broken DNA make breast cancers respond less to hormone therapy.
This project studies how myeloid cells from bone marrow affect whether virotherapy works against glioma.
This project studies how molecular mutations change blood-forming stem cells in myelodysplastic syndrome and builds a library of resources to share.
This project studies a mobile piece of genetic material that moves between cells in an oral bacterium, Streptococcus mutans, and how it affects disease.
This project builds a machine learning tool that uses oxygen saturation and blood flow features to screen newborns for congenital heart disease.
This project studies how immersive virtual reality works in chronic pain and compares it with how placebo pain relief works.
This project studies whether cellular senescence plays a role in artery damage from Doxorubicin chemotherapy, in mice and in cancer patients.
This project screens a library of natural compounds for ones that block a cancer-driving protein in precancerous cells, aiming to prevent colorectal cancer.
This project tests whether brain cells in the orbitofrontal cortex that reach the ventral striatum control how fast animals learn from errors.
This project studies how a transcription factor shapes the development of human veins, using human stem cells grown into vein cells.
This project studies how complement activation causes acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease, using animal models, microfluidics and human samples.
This project uses mathematics to study epigenetic regulation in human cells.
This project uses virtual reality and wearable devices to study how working with robots affects mental fatigue, attention and stress in construction workers.
This project studies molecular features of prostate cancer, builds ways to predict outcomes in men, and develops treatments to improve them.
This project studies how the innate immune system sees cells from a half-matched donor as foreign, which causes rejection of blood stem cell transplants.
This project builds an x-ray tube with several sources of radiation and uses it to make a faster computed tomography scanner.
This project develops MRI methods to image metabolic changes in brain tumors and guide surgery to remove them.
This project studies how physical activity, tiredness and thinking problems affect whether breast cancer survivors stay employed.
